definition: building by hand the sense of where my body is that other people get for free

settled:
Before dancing, my sense of where my body was ran weakly or not at all. I only realised about a year ago that I do not intrinsically know where my limbs are most of the time. It is what made me so clumsy as a child.

In college I took almost a major's worth of ballroom classes. That got me past the clumsiness.

The words came first: frame, axis, weight transfer, posture, head carriage. Each was a handle to check myself against while the pattern was still being built. Without them I would have been learning by imitation, which is the channel I do not have.

Then sheer volume, until it encoded and the checking fell away. The words are still there as a fallback, but by default the body runs on the trained weights.

It carried off the dance floor. At the missionary training centre I caught myself dancing while washing dishes, and it reached how I move through a room.

Nothing bound it to a dance floor, which is the same gap that made it expensive to build.

I still run into things often.

title: How I Learned To Feel My Body
